files.content: # Glass product recipe ## Look One invented object of glass, metal and light hangs in an endless dark studio. Strip lights behind it turn clear glass into thin bright outlines with rainbow edges, and its inner parts show through like a display case. A light sweep draws the contour before any content. Macro shots orbit slowly. An exploded view drifts apart and snaps shut on the downbeat; from that frame the object glows from within, light travels its channels and spreads over the floor on each beat. Subtitles sit in a frosted-glass slab. The name is an ultra-thin, widely tracked title with a glint. Screen holds only the object, its light and a few words. Long strips behind and beside the object trace the clear glass in thin white. Inner parts are the ornament: a rippled metal disc, spiral channels, a chrome hub, a board with gold traces. Motion is slow and exact. Every cut, sweep and pulse sits on a 120 BPM grid. The film turns once: the parts click together and the object starts emitting light. The object is always fictional. No real product silhouette, logo, typeface or interface. For any topic, ask what invisible thing the object does, then show it as light inside glass: a diffuser's mist, a battery's charge, a lesson's idea, a story's secret. Not this: a white catalogue shot, a wireframe HUD, a bullet-point slide, a 3D render with a floor horizon. Material and light are the subject. Keep the frame dark. ## How to draw it The example paints every view once at load with Canvas 2D (the source used a 3D engine), then only moves the pictures. Projection - The object is a stack of lathe parts in millimetres: dome 10 x 5.2, band r 10, disc r 5.8, ring r 7.5, spirals r 1.6-7.2, a frosted bowl, a foot. - A view = the axis direction plus a scale in px/mm. One affine `setTransform` turns each flat circle into an ellipse. Solids are the convex hull of their projected samples. - Views used: macro 3/4 from 30 degrees above; side macro with the face almost edge-on (face ellipse 0.4); exploded view with the axis about 45 degrees to the line of sight; near-front hero. Clear glass - Dark, faintly tinted band at the thick rim; clear middle. Alpha 0.12 at 62% of the radius, 0.5 at 86%, 0.78 at the rim. - 2 px bright outline. Two thin side-strip crescents plus a soft top-softbox crescent, clipped inside the silhouette. Two tiny speculars. - Rainbow on one side of the thick edge: three strokes, each 0.7% further inside. - Never paint a flat highlight over the middle. Metal - Satin band and brushed disc: conic gradients with bright lobes at the strip angles. - 46 concentric ripples on the disc, alternating light and dark. - Chrome hub: offset radial gradient plus a white speck. - Gold board traces at 45 degree steps. Frosted glass - It reads dark grey only because the edge is brighter than the centre. Radial gradient from strip colour into black: 10% at the middle, 42% just inside the edge. - The milky foot is the brightest solid. Light - Lit parts are separate pictures and overlays. Thick rim: a pastel band from `--utama` to `--aksen`. - Spiral channels keep a dark tube with a thin bright core. - Comet pulses run along the spirals (thin core) and the ring (core plus a wide faint glow) as SVG dashes: `pathLength="1"`, one CSS variable per group. - A soft halo behind the object breathes with the beat. Wave rings on the floor are scaled radial-gradient ellipses. Sweep - A soft vertical band: 14 degree tilt, 560 px wide, masked edges. It crosses the object and reveals a pre-drawn highlight picture (brighter outlines, a 20% wash of light over the dome, stronger rainbow). - Band moves, its content moves back by the same amount. The highlight stays put on the glass; only compositing happens. Background - Near-black with a dark radial sweep of `--latar-2` behind the object (lighter in the exploded view). - Paint the vignette into the backgrounds. Never put a full-screen overlay above moving layers. - No horizon line. No grain. ## Palette - `--latar`: studio black. `--latar-2`: radial sweep behind the object, the frosted slab, the satin dock. - `--utama` is the light the object emits: lit rim, channel pulses, halo, floor waves, the slab's top line. - `--aksen` is the second hue the light drifts toward (ice blue to violet in the source). These two are the only saturated colours on screen. - `--teks`: every title and slab line. `--teks-redup`: contact line. `--utama-di-latar`: price and the glint's leading edge. `--aksen-di-latar`: the glint's trailing edge. - Look tokens derived from the contract: `--cahaya` (strip-light white, 94% `--teks`) draws every outline, crescent and speck. On a pale brand the studio becomes bright-field photography and the glass turns into dark outlines on white. `--logam` (metal grey) fills band and disc. `--emas` (fixed gold, mixed 10% toward `--latar`) fills board traces. - Fixed for every brand: dispersion hues `--spek-1` orange, `--spek-2` green, `--spek-3` blue. Use them only on thick glass edges and in the sweep. Never on type or flat surfaces. ## Type - Name, `--font-judul`: Inter 400, 132 px (the thinnest grotesk bundled; the look wants ultra-thin). Tracking 0.46 em with matching left padding so it stays centred. Position y 104, upper third. - Glint: a 16%-wide band running `--utama-di-latar`, `--cahaya`, `--aksen-di-latar`. It crosses the letters left to right in 0.9 s, in step with the light sweep on the object. - Subtitle slab, `--font-isi`: Inter 400, 40 px, tracking 0.02 em, centred in a 76 px bar at y 912. Bar: radius 38, 80% `--latar-2`, 1.5 px inner line at 24% `--teks`, 2 px `--utama` to `--aksen` line along the top. - One short line, held at least 1.7 s, fading in and out over 0.2 s. Slogan 46 px. Contact 40 px, tracking 0.14 em. - No brand fonts: Inter, or Space Grotesk 500 for gadgets. Skip heavy display faces (Archivo Black, Bebas Neue); this look is thin and quiet. For a wider brand face, cut tracking before size. - Show at most one slab line or the name block at a time. Product names go in titles, never the slab. ## Beat and motion - 120 BPM: beat 0.5 s, bar 2 s. Cuts land on beats (here 2.5, 5, 10.5, 11.75 s). Sweeps, the snap and pulses are grid events. - The camera never stops, eased in-out. Macro push 1 to 1.07 over the shot with a 26 px pan. Side orbit is faked: roll -2.5 to +2.5 degrees, +-24 px pan, scale 1 to 1.05. - Sweeps: 0.45 s per beat in macro shots; 0.8-0.9 s for the opening and the title. Band opacity follows sin(pi*progress). - Opening: start almost black. The first sweep crosses immediately while the object fades up over 0.8 s. Contour first, content second. - Exploded view: one spread value e drives all parts. Apart in 3 s with cubic ease-out (e 0 to 1), hover 1.15 s while drifting to 1.03, then a 0.25 s cubic ease-in snap landing exactly on the downbeat. - Parts sit on the axis at fixed offsets (+40 to -32 mm), perspective 120/(120 - depth), so near parts grow and far parts shrink. - Tilt: `cos(i·2.3 + 0.9)·0.28` (times 40 degrees). Horizontal squash: 0.35 times |`sin(i·1.7 + 0.4)·0.32`|. Both scale with e. - Slow parallax orbit, +-0.6 px per mm of depth. The frame centre slides 140 px toward the far end as parts spread. - The snap: lit overlay and halo appear on the same frame. Flash decays as e^(-t/0.12). Camera shakes about two frames (22 px, decaying e^(-t/0.08)) then pushes in 40% over 0.9 s ease-out. - Pulses, per bar at [0, 0.75, 1, 1.5] s: a spiral comet travels centre to rim in 0.42 s; two ring comets leave one point in opposite directions at 0.6 turn/s, fading e^(-t/0.55); a floor wave grows at 55 mm/s, fading e^(-t/0.6). After the last hit the light settles and the comets loop slowly (ring: 0.22 turn/s). - Ending: macro pulls back 2.05x to 1x in 0.75 s ease-in-out. Name fades up in 0.5 s with its glint; slogan and contact follow 0.3 s and 0.35 s later (0.3 s fades). Hold 2 s. Fade to black over the last 0.4 s. ## Shot list - Sweep across a dark object with a slow push: outline arrives first. For an unknown thing, a teaser, a before-state. - Macro 3/4 from above, slow push: nothing hidden, the inside seen through glass. For an ingredient, a mechanism, a lesson's core idea. - Side macro orbit, face nearly edge-on: clear vs metal vs frosted. For build quality, layers, a seam, "handmade". - Exploded view on a diagonal, slow parallax: technical beauty, suspension. For what's inside, a parts list, the pause before the turn. - Snap plus 40% push-in: it comes together and wakes up. For the reveal, a class's "aha", a launch moment. - Straight-on front, slight push: a declaration. For one number, a name, the proof. - Top-down macro of the lit channels: the concept at full size. For energy, flow, data, scent. - Wave rings across the floor: the effect radiating outward. For range, reach, a community spreading. - Pull-back into dark space: room for type. For the call to action, the name, the slogan. Framing: a single hero, centred or placed on a strong diagonal, uncropped in wide shots (macro may crop). Shots need no spatial continuity. Link them with hard cuts on the beat or a sweep through black. No dissolves, no wipes. ## Signature moves - Contour before content: black frame, a sweep crosses and leaves the outline, then the interior fades up. A small perfumery's new glass bottle; a creator teasing next week's gadget review; a science teacher asking "what is inside this?"; the opening shot of a mystery story. - Transparency: macro through the clear dome onto the inner part (rippled disc, spirals, gold traces). A watch repairer showing a movement; a skincare serum's layered capsule; a physics class peering into a speaker; a glass locked box in a story. - Dispersion edge: a sweep over the thick rim becomes a travelling rainbow. A prism lamp; a lens maker's workshop; a photography channel on chromatic aberration; a fairy-tale crystal. - Exploded view and snap: parts float apart along the axis with a counter in the slab, hover, then snap shut on the downbeat. "9 parts, all washable" for a diffuser; a modular backpack; a teacher breaking an idea into steps; plot pieces clicking together. - Light that travels inside: after the snap, comets run through the channels and the rim glows. Mist lighting up; a battery charging; a router's data; a lesson idea spreading through a class. - Waves on the floor: every beat sends a ring of light across the floor. A speaker's range; a scent's trail; a creator's reach; news travelling through a village story. - Thin title with glint: ultra-thin tracked caps, glint riding the last sweep. A product name; a course title; a channel's season name; a short film's title card. ## Pitfalls - Performance in live preview: paint each view once (a few canvases, about 0.5 s at load), convert to ``, and animate only images and two small SVGs. Never animate a blur or `backdrop-filter`; the frosted slab is a translucent fill, not a live blur. The sweep moves a masked band and counter-moves its content. Never animate a mask position or redraw the glass. - Glass on black turns black. Without edges and crescents clear glass vanishes; without a brighter rim frosted glass looks like plastic. Keep the dome's middle clear. - Colour: a single light family. Dispersion on thick edges only. No gradient on type except the momentary glint. Idle light is off; the object stays dark until the snap. - Edge-on exploded view: an axis perpendicular to the view flattens discs into lines. Hold it near 45 degrees so discs read as ellipses (0.6-0.7). - Profiles can read as mushrooms or plates. Use 3/4 or near-edge-on side views, and few concentric bright rings at the dome base (one band, not three). - Light brands: `--cahaya` follows `--teks`, so on white the glass becomes dark outlines (bright-field). Confirm the slab, name and price still read, and that the lit band is not the only thing marking the object. - Type: nothing in the bottom 80 px or within 120 px of the sides; the slab at y 912 is the lowest line. Seven words on screen, maximum. ## Reference numbers - Reference excerpt: 12 s at 24 fps, 4 shots, cuts at 2.0, 9.0 and 10.0 s, an internal change at 4.0 s (median shot 2 s, 15 cuts a minute). Motion energy peaks in the last shot, once the light is on. - Colour sampled per shot: macro #010102 (69%), #161b1f (17%), #3e3e3f, #717475. Exploded #020306, #14181d, #44474b, #9097a5. Lit #1e2738, #585e80, #9fa6e0 (lavender light, 6-11%). Source accent: ice blue #62dcff to violet #a98bff. The example uses these as defaults. - Example order: macro, side macro, exploded, snap and glow, front, lit macro. Stretched 1.25x to 15 s, ending pulled back to leave room for the name. ## Free choices Pick the object (always fictional), its internals, the light colour, opening, ending and pace. - Structure options: line-up of three variants judged by their inner glow; a day in light, with the strip kit rotating round one object; a material stack, peeling one layer per beat down to the core. - Opening options: inside first (a single inner part, shell grows around it); caustic first (light on the floor, traced back up to the object); silhouettes (a few dark outlines, one starts to glow). - Ending options: floor only (object exits, its wave goes on pulsing); cool down (glow dims to bare strip outlines); held macro (no pull-back, one detail, a small name).

# Glass product: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 1.25, medium 2.5, long 5.

## hook

- en: black frame; a light sweep draws the object's glass contour, then its inside shows through as the camera pushes in
- id: layar hitam; sapuan lampu menggambar tepi kaca benda, lalu isinya terlihat sambil kamera mendekat

## problem

- en: the object stays dark and frosted, only a dim outline; one sweep shows what is missing
- id: benda tetap gelap dan buram, hanya garis tepinya; satu sapuan memperlihatkan apa yang kurang

## fact

- en: side macro orbit: clear glass, metal band and frosted shell side by side; a rainbow runs along the thick edge
- id: makro samping mengorbit: kaca bening, pita logam, dan cangkang buram berdampingan; pelangi berjalan di tepi tebal

## step

- en: one part lifts out along the axis per step and floats, lit by a sweep, while the subtitle slab names it
- id: tiap langkah satu bagian terangkat di sumbunya dan melayang, disapu lampu, bilah subtitle menyebut namanya

## compare

- en: the same object twice in one dark studio, cut on the beat; the better one lights up from inside
- id: benda yang sama dua kali di studio gelap, dipotong pada ketukan; yang lebih baik menyala dari dalam

## number

- en: exploded view on a diagonal; the subtitle slab counts the parts, then they snap shut on the downbeat
- id: tampilan terurai di diagonal; bilah subtitle menghitung bagiannya, lalu semuanya merapat tepat pada ketukan

## proof

- en: front hero: the light ring races inside the glass and a wave spreads over the floor on every beat
- id: tampak depan: cincin cahaya berlari di dalam kaca, gelombang menyebar di lantai pada tiap ketukan

## offer

- en: straight-on front with a slight push; the price stands as an ultra-thin tracked title above it
- id: tampak depan dengan dorongan pelan; harga berdiri sebagai judul super tipis berspasi lebar di atasnya

## cta

- en: the macro pulls back into dark space; ultra-thin name with a glint, slogan and contact, held 2 s
- id: makro mundur ke ruang gelap; nama super tipis dengan kilau, slogan, dan kontak, diam 2 detik

## payoff

- en: the same sweep as the opening, now over an object glowing by itself; name small, held 2 s
- id: sapuan yang sama seperti pembuka, kini di atas benda yang menyala sendiri; nama kecil, diam 2 detik

        box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px color-mix(in oklab, var(--teks) 24%, transparent); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
      .pill::before { content: ""; position: absolute; left: 40px; right: 40px; top: 2px; height: 2px;

      .kilau { position: absolute; inset: 0; padding-left: 0.46em; color: transparent; background-size: 300% 100%; background-position: 100% 0;
        background-image: linear-gradient(100deg, transparent 42%, color-mix(in oklab, var(--utama-di-latar) 70%, transparent) 47%, var(--cahaya) 50%, color-mix(in oklab, var(--aksen-di-latar) 70%, transparent) 53%, transparent 58%);

      // Warna token dibaca lewat kanvas, jadi gambar kaca ikut brand.

      const rgb = (n) => { probe.style.color = `var(${n})`; px.clearRect(0, 0, 1, 1); px.fillStyle = getComputedStyle(probe).color; px.fillRect(0, 0, 1, 1); return [...px.getImageData(0, 0, 1, 1).data.slice(0, 3)]; };
      const [L, D, S, U, A, G, M, ...RB] = ["--cahaya", "--latar", "--latar-2", "--utama", "--aksen", "--emas", "--logam", "--spek-1", "--spek-2", "--spek-3"].map(rgb);
      probe.remove();
      const mix = (a, b, t) => a.map((v, i) => v + (b[i] - v) * t), C = (c, al = 1) => `rgba(${c.map(Math.round)},${al})`, DL = (t) => mix(D, L, t);
